source_metadata.title: Testosterone therapy in older men: clinical implications of recent landmark trials

atoms.canonical_statement: The invited narrative review aims to synthesize the major benefits, risks, and clinical implications of recent large placebo-controlled testosterone trials in middle-aged and older men with possible hypogonadism but no identifiable HPT-axis pathology.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we discuss the salient findings of these trials and provide our perspective on how they inform “personalized decision-making”

atoms.canonical_statement: The review focuses on testosterone trials that enrolled at least 300 men, were placebo controlled, provided at least 1 year of therapy, and assessed clinically important outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: large (enrolling at least 300 men), placebo-controlled, and had at least 1 year of therapy with assessment of clinically important outcomes

atoms.canonical_statement: The review is a narrative synthesis and does not report a systematic search strategy, formal study-selection flow, or formal risk-of-bias assessment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We review here the major findings and clinical implications

atoms.canonical_statement: The review describes TEAAM as a placebo-controlled testosterone trial in 308 men using Testosterone 75 mg transdermal gel daily, dose adjusted, for 3 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: N = 308 ≥ 60 years

population.label: TEAAM participants: men age 60 years or older with serum total testosterone 3.47-13.9 nmol/L and no identifiable HPT-axis pathology

concept.text: Testosterone 75 mg transdermal gel daily, dose adjusted, for 3 years

atoms.canonical_statement: The review describes T-Trials as a placebo-controlled testosterone trial in 790 men using Testosterone 50 mg transdermal gel daily, dose adjusted to the normal range, for 1 year.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: N = 790 ≥ 65 years

population.label: T-Trials participants: men age 65 years or older with serum total testosterone at or below approximately 9.5 nmol/L plus symptoms or signs of testosterone deficiency and no identifiable HPT-axis pathology

concept.text: Testosterone 50 mg transdermal gel daily, dose adjusted to the normal range, for 1 year

atoms.canonical_statement: The review describes T4DM as a placebo-controlled testosterone trial in 1007 men using Intramuscular testosterone undecanoate 1000 mg at weeks 0 and 6 then every 3 months for 2 years plus a community lifestyle programme.

population.label: T4DM participants: men age 50-74 years with serum total testosterone at or below 14 nmol/L and impaired glucose tolerance or newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, without identifiable HPT-axis pathology

concept.text: Intramuscular testosterone undecanoate 1000 mg at weeks 0 and 6 then every 3 months for 2 years plus a community lifestyle programme
Placebo injections plus the same community lifestyle programme

atoms.canonical_statement: The review describes TRAVERSE as a placebo-controlled testosterone trial in 5246 men using Dose-adjusted transdermal testosterone gel, target serum testosterone 12.1-26.0 nmol/L and haematocrit <=54%, for up to 4 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: TRAVERSE N = 5246

population.label: TRAVERSE participants: men age 45-80 years with serum total testosterone >3.5 to <=10.4 nmol/L, symptoms or signs of testosterone deficiency, and high or pre-existing cardiovascular risk, without identifiable HPT-axis pathology

concept.text: Dose-adjusted transdermal testosterone gel, target serum testosterone 12.1-26.0 nmol/L and haematocrit <=54%, for up to 4 years

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports that TEAAM found no effect of testosterone therapy on health-related quality of life measured with SF-36.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: testosterone therapy had no effect on health-related quality of life measured by the full SF-36 questionnaire

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports that the T-Trials vitality primary outcome was not significantly improved, although men with low vitality had a significant improvement in SF-36 vitality (P=.03) and secondary analyses showed small average benefits in vitality and mood.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: subgroup of men with baseline low vitality and mood had a significantly improved a SF-36 vitality score (P = .03)

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports that T4DM found no effect of testosterone therapy on SF-36 health-related quality of life.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In T4DM, testosterone therapy had no effect on measures of health-related quality of life

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports that TRAVERSE showed modest but significant improvements in mood and energy in men with and without significant depressive symptoms, without improvement in sleep quality.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: testosterone therapy caused modest but significant improvements in mood and energy, but not in sleep quality

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports that the T-Trials Cognitive Function substudy did not improve memory or cognitive function in men with self-reported age-related memory impairment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: testosterone therapy did not improve memory or cognitive function of men with self-reported, age-related memory impairment

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports an exploratory T-Trials analysis showing improved executive function when all randomized men were analyzed, a finding the authors state requires confirmation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: there was a significant improvement of executive function when all men in the T-Trials were included

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports no detectable clinically significant cognitive benefit from testosterone therapy in TEAAM.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In TEAAM and TRAVERSE, there were no detectable clinically significant effects of testosterone therapy on cognitive function

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors conclude that in symptomatic men with serum testosterone at or below 10.4 nmol/L, testosterone therapy modestly improves vitality and mood but has no established cognitive benefit; these modest mood/energy effects are generally insufficient as the sole reason to initiate therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: testosterone therapy modestly improves vitality (energy) and mood, but has no effect on cognitive function

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports no improvement in sexual function measures with testosterone therapy in TEAAM.

population.label: TRAVERSE participants: men age 45-80 years with serum total testosterone >3.5 to <=10.4 nmol/L, symptoms or signs of testosterone deficiency, and high or pre-existing cardiovascular risk, without identifiable HPT-axis pathology

concept.text: Dose-adjusted transdermal testosterone gel, target serum testosterone 12.1-26.0 nmol/L and haematocrit <=54%, for up to 4 years

quantitative_result.original_result_text: acute kidney injury was slightly more common in the testosterone group (60 vs 40 men, P = .04)

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors conclude that available trial data do not indicate increased de novo prostate-cancer or BPH-with-LUTS risk, but testosterone raises PSA and may increase prostate-cancer evaluations and urinary-retention risk in men with more severe LUTS.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: testosterone therapy increases the risk of an evaluation for prostate cancer due to increased serum PSA

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors caution that several reported testosterone effects were secondary rather than primary trial outcomes and that subgroup analyses require caution.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: some effects of testosterone treatment discussed in this review are secondary rather than primary trial outcomes

atoms.canonical_statement: The trials synthesized in the review lasted no more than 4 years, leaving longer-term cardiovascular and prostate outcomes insufficiently characterized.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the trials included in this review were ≤4 years duration

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors advocate personalized decision-making that weighs modest potential benefits in energy, libido, anemia, glucose metabolism, physical function, and bone against small or uncertain risks including pulmonary embolism, traumatic fracture, PSA-triggered evaluation, erythrocytosis, and urinary retention.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: These data help inform “personalized decision-making”

atoms.canonical_statement: Pending further trials, the authors recommend a holistic men’s-health approach emphasizing healthy lifestyle behaviors and assessment and treatment of other risk factors and diseases.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a holistic approach to men’s health, including encouragement of healthy lifestyle behaviours, and assessment and attention to risk factors and disease, should remain the universal approach

extraction_limitations: The evaluated source is an invited narrative review, while the governing LiteratureAtom model is designed for primary literature.
Trial-result atoms therefore represent the review’s secondary report of underlying trials; they are tagged secondary_reported_result and anchored to the review, not to the cited primary publications.
No missing denominators, effect estimates, trial details, or recommendation strength were invented. Quantitative fields were populated only when the review reported a defensible measure.
No cited primary trial was independently verified during @ATOM; current regulatory verification was performed only for the separate @SEA currency check.
